content:
sarah.support: Heads up — user reported a payment flow hit the autorouter and it returned the order_status tool instead of creating a refund. High priority, customer waiting.

mike.eng: Which API call / payload? any errors in logs?

sarah.support: Here's the POST we got from the web UI (sanitized):
```json
{
  "customer_id": "cust_12345",
  "intent": "refund",
  "reason": "product damaged"
  // notice: amount & currency omitted (UI left them blank)
}
```
No explicit error returned, router just routed to `order_status`.

jessica-ml: Router-bot probably matches on intent and domain. If amount missing, the refund signature (which requires amount+currency) may have been lower confidence than the simpler `order_status` signature.

router-bot: Automated note: autoroute_v2 evaluated signatures -> order_status confidence 0.78, refund_tool_v1 confidence 0.41. Fallback applied.

alex-devex: Can we reproduce quickly with a curl payload? I can try local autorouter with the same payload.

mike.eng: Please paste the full route decision log (from the router service) if available. We need to see feature flags and signature scores.

sarah.support: Attaching excerpt from logs below (scrubbed):
```
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] request_id=rq_9a3 auth_ok customer_id=cust_12345 intent=refund payload_size=186
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] router: signatures_matched=[order_status(customer_id), refund_tool(amount,currency,customer_id)]
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] router: scores={order_status:0.78, refund_tool:0.41}
[2026-03-15T13:02:11Z] router: selected=order_status reason=highest_confidence
```
jessica-ml: Confirmed — refund_tool signature requires (amount,currency). Missing fields penalize its score heavily. We should return a validation error upstream instead of silently routing.

mike.eng: Agreed. Current behavior is: autorouter treats missing required schema fields as low-confidence rather than hard-invalid. That lets it pick a different tool. Bad for UX.

alex-devex: Short-term mitigation: increase required-field penalty for refund_tool to -INF (i.e., hard fail) so missing amount/currency causes no match. Long-term: surface a proper 4xx schema validation error to clients when required args are missing.

sarah.support: Customer wants a fix now — can we rollback to previous router heuristic or apply the required-field hard-fail change?

mike.eng: I can patch the matcher config to make refund_tool's amount+currency required. Will do a canary to 10% of traffic for 30m.

prod-monitor-bot: Deploy started: config_update/matcher v2026-03-15-07 -> canary 10% at 13:18 UTC.

jessica-ml: Also add a note in the console: "If refund requests omit amount/currency the request will be rejected" so support+UI teams can validate before submit.

sarah.support: Once patched, please post the canary result and example response the client will see. Need it to close the ticket.

mike.eng: Canary rolled out. Observing 0.6% error spike (expected). Route decisions after patch show refund_tool score=NA (required fields missing) and router now returns 400 schema_error for those requests. Example response: ```json
{
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "message": "refund missing required fields: amount, currency"
}
```

sarah.support: Will relay to customer. Any follow-ups?

alex-devex: Plan: (1) update autorouter docs about strict schema match for billing tools, (2) add client-side UI validation to prevent blank amount fields, (3) add a targeted eval to detect ambiguous signature collisions (refund vs status) and surface a warning.

jessica-ml: Also schedule a model-signature review next week to find other tools with similar overlaps.

sarah.support: Thanks all — marking as in-progress for support until customer confirms. :white_check_mark:

prod-monitor-bot: Canary metrics: error_rate(normalized)=+0.6% (transient), selected_fallback_rate for billing decreased by 94%.

mike.eng: We'll promote config to 100% in 2 hours if no regression.

sarah.support: Closing loop: customer confirmed they received a helpful validation error and updated UI. Issue resolved on their side. Reopen if recurrence.

alex-devex: Filed follow-up RFC: "autorouter: strict schema enforcement for billing and payment tools" — tracking id RFC-2026-42.

sarah.support: Nice work :tada:
